# Here begins the Geomancy published by | Master Gerard of Cremona <note>Gerard of Cremona (c. 1114–1187) was a famous translator of Arabic scientific works into Latin.</note>

**W**hoever desires to know strictly through **geomancy** <note>A method of divination that interprets markings on the ground or patterns formed by tossed handfuls of soil/rocks.</note> concerning present particulars and future things, let him seek with his whole heart's affection from God—who is the inspector of all future things—that He might grant him to arrive at a knowledge of those things he intends to ask, through the judgments of this art, which [proceeds] through the preceding time as a mother toward them.

**S**eeing, therefore, that it is not sufficient to contemplate this geomancy entirely apart from the secret counsel of God—for the secrets of God can be foreknown by no mortal, indeed, not all mortality together may behold them—truly, He willed that the spirit of the Creator, created in His own likeness, should be excluded from ignorance. Just as He protected man so that ignorance would not remain hidden, He also gathered the refuge of science for one wishing to rise after the Fall.
And it is by the disposition of the Divine Will that many, in this light of our lightning-flash <note>Likely referring to human intellect or sudden insight</note>, have reached out from this earth toward the unseen, and with an ample mind have measured the space of the intervals of the heavens and the circles of the spheres by the probable reasoning of a number of stages. They contemplate the globes of the stars and the revolutions of the firmament, and the course of the **Zodiac** with its inhabitants, through the sharp edge of the intellect. Again, they consider the volume of the eight [spheres] which the golden praises of the poets make known: the receptions, the aspects of the houses, and the glory of the boundaries made in the zodiac by the knowledge of signs.

**W**hich science, since it does not disagree with descending truth, [is] a fragrance for the inner senses...

<column-break/>

...of many, it hears how many lustrations <note>Purification rituals or cycles of time</note> have been offered by those laboring under the stars, which also handed down the course of the planets and the creation in the world below. We read also that the **Patriarch Abraham** <note>In medieval tradition, Abraham was often regarded as a great astrologer and the father of hidden sciences.</note> held this art under the astronomy of the Egyptians; for if it had not been established in truth, he would not have approached it as a primary cause. If the flight of birds or every sign of the stars is significant, the will of that One who ordains all things by judgment is not without merit. In truth and in memory, both in **astronomy** and in **geomancy**, He is seen to be especially entreated.

**N**ow, if anyone desires to predict anything through geomancy and does not wish to be deceived, let him hold to the right path in which this point of prayer is maintained: that he should not look upon the matter except with a ready mind, nor presume to judge in a state of disturbance or mere opinion.

**F**or it is a matter of such great levity among certain men that immediately after a question has been negligently made, they deliver a judgment; and when they have fallen into [error in] judgment, which often happens, they would prefer to have remained silent. Thence it happens that because of their own negligence or rashness, the whole art is punished, which in itself contains nothing of a lie. Alas, the unlearned disciple suffers punishment, while the art itself is glory; for the truth is trodden underfoot and seen as a crime.

**G**eomancy is, however, just as an art [derived] from the knowledge of truth... <note>The text breaks off here, continuing the definition of the art.</note>

To whom should he present his judgments? Only to those of a sound mind, for no one reaches the summit if they are clouded by darkness. But let them also know that he assists through probable reason, lest anything be left to negligence, as has been said. For when the trials of the mind are not dominated by a false order, he who sees through the signs made for him ought to return a cautious medical remedy <note>The author likens astrological consultation to a medical diagnosis or "remedy" for the soul</note>. From this, the artist <note>term: artist (artifex) — here meaning a skilled practitioner of the "liberal art" of astrology</note> should not deceitfully provide a pretext for the slander of the world.

Therefore, he who seeks to know all things investigates with diligent inquiry; and when he has matured, and afterwards with God's help, he approaches the judgment through the aid of reason. These things are now concerning all the integrity of the faithful, if it is consulted at any time. When great matters are to be known, or when they are to be amplified, then the resolution of the matter excels. Since the names of others are outside the order—as when some perform a prophecy with another—it is useful to begin from the very inception of how they are made.

**H**aving therefore the knowledge of this art, we use the signs of the figures and the mansions of the houses. First, the certainty of the artists: for they are arranged in a certain order. The signs, however, are divided from here, where each figure has its own language in the special works, which leads us to the particularity of its individual understanding; and because the planets are positioned in the signs, they express the power, genus, and cause of the figures or the houses.

<column-break/>

The planets are seven: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon. The twelve dwellings of these planets are described by the authors, which we call by the names of the signs, of which there are twelve names: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces. 

First, let us see how the intellectual philosophers divided the firmament, and why it was not divided into a number other than twelve, nor into more or fewer parts of the heaven. To this, the wise men responded that they chose the number twelve by considering it as the multiplication of four by three, or three by four. For that number divides the motion of the whole into parts, excluding the diagonal. Now it is shown concerning the three by four, or the three by three, or the four. For it arises from the multiplication of six by two. But they sought why it should be from four by three or three by four, as we said, and not from others. 

Only why the philosophers chose so many planets and times of the heaven, and why they decreed this firmament to be twelve through three, and why not more than three if it seems so. For if the heaven was composed from a distribution, the matter is seen. All these things, if one looks at philosophy, Paul <note>likely a reference to St. Paul or a specific commentator named Paulus</note> undoubtedly did not wish to remain in such a principle, because the wise men divided the firmament into twelve parts.

We have divided the measurement four times four, as has been said, and they are called the 12 signs. Although [the sun] follows at a distance in the first part and is gradually let in, they can be equal. For it would be a cross <note>original: "crux"; likely meaning a point of confusion or difficulty</note> if anyone spoke unless more were added, because it would not be known whether it was in the beginning, middle, or end of the sign itself. For this reason, I have delayed [explaining] how they divided the parts of the earth into countless pieces. Each sign is one thing, which they divided into 30 parts that we call degrees <term>gradus: the 360 degrees of a circle</term>. When the number of signs and degrees are brought together, they become 360 in total. This division principally delivers nothing [else]; the number twelve is observed with devotion in the division. Moreover, just as that half part, so also the rest. That is, if one divides 360 degrees through the middle, it will hold 180, which are the degrees of 6 signs, which is the middle part of 12. Also, if one divides this by a third, he will have 120 from these, which are the degrees of 4 signs <note>The scribe likely means the degrees for 4 signs total 120</note>, which is the [third] part of 12. And if he divides by 4, he will have the degrees of three signs, which is the 4th part of 12. And therefore, if he divides by ten <note>The text says "denarium" (ten), but the math for 60 degrees suggests a division by six</note>, you will have 60, which are the degrees of two signs, which stands as the 6th part of 12.

**F**or this reason, therefore, they divided the zodiac, as has been said, into 12 parts, which, stretching from the north to the south, encircles the sky in a flowing circuit, kindled with round stars. The earth, as has been said, is known by name to God alone, who counts the stars, since He alone knows their names, signs, powers, courses, places, and times. Wisely, however, they imposed other names of the world or of men upon them, so that 

<column-break/>

they might be more easily distinguished by men. These are called the images of the zodiac because they say the signs always have different names; "zodiac" in Greek is "of animals" in Latin <note>original: "animalatum"; the Greek *zodiakos* refers to a circle of small animals/figures</note>.

The first sign is Aries, which consists of many stars. According to the fables, it is named for the Golden Fleece that carried Helle across the sea <note>The myth of Phrixus and Helle</note>. It is placed there because just as the ram [sleeps] on its right side all winter and on its left side [in summer], they say the sun, traveling under that sign, opens the right part of the heaven.

->**T**he second is Taurus, because<-
Jupiter, in the abduction of Europa, was seen to be carried in the form of a bull. It is placed as a sign because the sun, positioned under that sign, lifts its rays into "horns" and now makes the land arable <note>A wordplay on *Taurus* (bull) and the use of oxen for plowing</note>.

The third is Gemini: Castor and Pollux, the sons of Jupiter. From a crowd of stars, it is made starry <gloss>starred</gloss> as a sign, placed because the sun lingers under that sign for two days more than under any other.

**T**he fourth is Cancer, which, as they say, was sent by Neptune against Hercules and was crushed by his foot. It is therefore made starry <gloss>starred</gloss>. It is placed as a sign because just as the crab walks backward, so the sun, having reached that sign, turns its course back.

The fifth sign is Leo, which was the greatest [beast] slain by the arms of Hercules. Therefore it is starry <gloss>starred</gloss>. It is placed there because just as the lion rules in the middle [of the beasts], so the heat of nature is imposed [in midsummer].

# The Signs of the Zodiac and the Planets

The sun, being in that sign <note>likely referring to Leo from the previous page</note> in the month of August, makes it hot, while in another it makes it cold.

**T**he sixth sign is the Virgin, namely Erigone, the daughter of Icarius <note>In Greek mythology, Erigone was transformed into the constellation Virgo</note>. She was taken up entirely into the stars because of the sign given by her father; and just as she remained a virgin and did not give birth, so this sign brings forth the month of September.
---
The seventh is the Scales <note>Latin: *Libra*</note>, which signifies the justice of the King's daughter. Because of the equality of her justice, she is the goddess of the scales, by which the life of men is weighed. It represents the autumn season because at that time the sun makes the equinox <note>original: *equinoctium*</note> as it travels under that sign.

**T**he eighth is the Scorpion, which struck the giant Orion and destroyed him. Because of this, he was placed among the stars. This sign is placed in the autumn season because in that month, words are often found to be false rather than true <note>A medieval metaphorical link between the scorpion's sting and deceitful speech</note>.
---
The ninth is the Archer <note>Latin: *Sagittarius*</note>, who is Chiron the Centaur. He is depicted with a bow because he shot his own son <note>The scribe may be conflating various myths here regarding Chiron and the sting of the Scorpion</note>. He is said to be of the forest, and under this sign the victims of the hunt are sought, as the weather turns toward better things.

**T**he tenth is Capricorn. When Jupiter was a small child, he was cast out by his father and raised by a goat, which was later placed among the stars. This sign is so named because just as a goat climbs high places, so the sun then shows itself at the heights of heaven. Its tail ends in a point, signifying the end of the month and the rainy season.
---
The eleventh is the Water-Bearer <note>Latin: *Aquarius*</note>, namely Ganymede, the son of the Trojan king.

<column-break/>

He was loved by Jupiter and taken up into heaven as a reward. It is said that when the sun is here, clouds are released and the weather is rainy.

**T**he twelfth is the Fishes <note>Latin: *Pisces*</note>. For when the giant Typhon was pursuing the gods, Cupid and his mother <note>Venus</note> came to Egypt and hid there in the form of fishes. For this reason, the people there did not eat fish for a long time, lest they accidentally devour the gods. These two were made into a constellation. This sign is also rainy.

Within these parts of the signs wander the seven planets, whose divine power governs all things in the world. They are held within the firmament which rotates from east to west. The first planet from the earth is the Moon, which generates coldness and humidity. It travels through all the signs of the zodiac in its cycle. <note>The text here contains abbreviations regarding the timing of the lunar cycle</note>.

The second is Mercury, which is associated with Jupiter <note>The text is slightly garbled here regarding the "malice" or "nature" of the planet</note>. It runs through the signs in 30 days.

The third is Venus, a feminine planet by nature, generating a temperament of coldness and moisture. It passes through the signs in 369 days.

The fourth is the Sun, which stands apart from the others because of the greatness of its light. It works with heat and dryness, flying through the zodiac in 365 days.

The fifth is Mars, of a hot and dry nature. It generates heat and dryness and passes through the signs in 2 years.

The sixth is Jupiter, a temperate planet, generating heat and humidity. It completes the zodiac in 12 years.

The seventh is Saturn, a cold and dry planet, generating dryness and heaviness.

# On the Houses and Exaltations of the Planets

In the 10th month, the Head <note>original: *Caput*; referring to the North Node of the Moon</note> or the Dragon's Tail <note>original: *dragonis*; the South Node</note> signifies ruin when they fall away from the planets, for they are not counted among them.

**B**eyond the planets, two signs are attributed to each as a domicile <note>The "home" sign where a planet's influence is strongest</note>, both for glory and for their kingdom. It is like a natural court. To the Sun, however, only one domicile is given, which is Leo. Likewise to the Moon, only one: namely, Cancer. These are understood in two ways: the sign in which the planet first appeared as a light above the firmament, or that which the planet rules according to the natural order. Since the planets generate various effects, they are distinguished by these verses:

The Sun here has its lodging and is placed in its seat;
Aries is its glory, while Libra is the place where it falls.
The Moon holds Cancer, which it has held for many years;
In Aries it has no power, but Scorpio strongly presses it.
And again, Taurus holds it, while Pisces holds it not.
Gemini can be its joy, and the Virgin goddess <note>Virgo</note> too.
Cancer and the Sea <note>Pisces</note> generate what reigns therein;
Leo itself commands, and the true rule is given.
Acacia <note>likely a corruption or specific plant-term used as a mnemonic</note> flourishes, Aries signifies it;
But in Libra, its power falls and becomes weaker.
Those things are moved by the net, with Pisces and Sagittarius;
And again, the Goat <note>Capricorn</note> casts down its evil glory.
Pisces holds Saturn, who has his highest place there;
And again, Aries is always his glory in Libra.

->In which signs each planet<-
->rejoices in its own house according to nature<-

Saturn rejoices in Aquarius. Jupiter in Sagittarius. Mars in Scorpio. Venus in Taurus. Mercury in Virgo. The Sun in Leo. Likewise, regarding exaltations <note>Specific degrees where a planet is most powerful</note>: Saturn is exalted in the 21st degree of Libra. Jupiter in the 15th of Cancer. Mars in the 28th of Capricorn. Venus in the 27th of Pisces. Mercury in the 15th of Virgo. The Head of the Dragon in the 3rd of Gemini. The Tail in the 3rd of Sagittarius. The Moon, however, in the 10th degree of Taurus.

<column-break/>

It is exalted in that place where it is stronger. In whatever sign it is free, it holds its right or its latitude through its own motion. It is said by the learned that the sign which follows is the place where the planet's power is expanded. The exaltation of all the zodiac is directed by these explanations.

**T**herefore, by the seasonal revolution, sixteen figures <note>The 16 figures of geomancy</note> are made known to us through this science, which are powerful among the planets and signs of the stars. The rest is gathered from the names of the accidents <note>technical term for non-essential qualities</note>, which are distinguished in the said vision. The disposition of the signs and planets is proportioned to the others; these are not chosen by whim, but grow from the certain confluence of the planets and other stars, as proven by judgment. These are as follows:

<margin>**Square of four dots** <note>The geomantic figure *Amissio* or *Acquisitio*—here likely *Acquisitio* (Gain)</note></margin>
Strongly, like a dear sign, it makes its nature from Aquarius in a medium sign; the nature of Jupiter and Venus signifies a good sign.

<margin>**Two dots vertically** <note>The geomantic figure *Fortuna Minor* or *Major*</note></margin>
Joy, the head is high or it lasts; the signs of Jupiter in Sagittarius are exalted in a benevolent sign.

<margin>**Three dots (two over one)** <note>The geomantic figure *Puella* (Girl)</note></margin>
Warlike, or a yellow girl; the signs of the Virgin <note>Virgo</note> are its nature, with the Moon's part in a malevolent sign.

<margin>**Four dots (three over one)** <note>The geomantic figure *Fortuna Major* (Greater Fortune)</note></margin>
Greater Fortune, tinted above all others; the sign of the Sun's glory in a benevolent sign.

<margin>**Two dots horizontally** <note>The geomantic figure *Conjunctio* (Conjunction)</note></margin>
Comprehension, strongly or exactly; the signs of Venus fall here, generating a bond.

In the case of *Victorious* <note>original: "victonum", likely referring to the figure Fortuna Major</note>, it signifies simplicity and confession. *The People* <note>original: "populus"</note> is a sign of change in the inner parts, of elations, rumors, and shifts. The *Head of the Dragon* <term>Caput Draconis: the North Node of the Moon, considered a point of increase and gain</term> signifies nobility, profit, a face of praise and acceptance, and mental clarity. These are the 16 signs which are placed through the 12 astrological houses <note>original: "domicilia astrologica"</note> according to the diverse ways of the art; for what is said here is how things must be known so that a response may be given to one wishing to be judged with discretion.

## The First House
is of birth and the life of man, or his name; it is remembered for anything in his life. It is judged specifically regarding his arrival, his knowledge, the color of bodies, character, knowledge, and the virtue received by the soul of the seeker. It measures a certain height between the divine, like the passage of a child enclosed in its mother who, born according to time, proceeds from darkness into light. Thus, the pulse from the heart is known just as a sign which arises is afterwards revealed.

## The Second House
signifies substance, both movable and all wealth, gifts, receivers, and the effect of things sought; it also signifies buyers, sellers, business, and those things which are moved from place to place.

## The Third House
is of brothers, sisters, neighbors, and kinsmen, and their help. It signifies a good journey or a praiseworthy friendship, and through the same it signifies letters, messengers, rumors, those whispering secret business, and the changing of those matters.

## The Fourth House
signifies the father,

<column-break/>

inheritance, the field, vineyards, trees, countryside, the things growing from the earth, and cultivation; it also signifies parentage. It relates to a city, castles, and all buildings, as well as income, death, and things hidden or concealed in the bowels of the earth. It signifies fidelity and friendship, and that which is truthful from the dead, and his burial; it looks toward the path and the end to the end of the life of the matter, according to how it is judged.

## The Fifth House
is of joy; it signifies messengers, children, and pregnant women, or testimonies, charters, books, and all things that are honest. It signifies desires, honors, petitions, a beloved woman, fruits, greenery, and places removed from the city by a distance, or the truth and the care of rivers and waters.

## Sixth House
is of infirmity, as it regards one's servants, small animals that are not present, the house of disgrace, loss, deceit, and craftiness; it also signifies justice and distant changes.

## The Seventh is the House
of wives and detractions; for it concerns the work of the court which is found or opposed in contests. It signifies the end of a report, the immunity of a partner, the wife of the court, and the business of visiting, or buying and selling. It signifies the same as mentioned in the second house: the pleas of all people, the fugitive, the thief, the lost, the exile, and the way to wherever.

## The Eighth House
is of doubt and fears, of passion, debt, and death; it concerns possession and dividing, and any labor and fear. It signifies the estates of those stretched out <note>likely referring to the deceased</note>, and it leads to warlike and attentive helpers, from which state of stewardship the cleverness of the mind varies and according to where life tends from here.

The **ninth house** is that of faith and religion; furthermore, it concerns the rational mind and the <term>stoles of wisdom</term> <note>original: "stolarum sapientiae," likely a metaphor for the garments or layers of deep knowledge</note>, greatness, honor, and the mastery of laws. It signifies the followers of God and all houses of religion, books of philosophy, true wisdom, and the arts. It also reveals the study of prayers and arts, scholarly letters, and messengers. It reveals dreams with full truth, then the "daughter of the East" <note>A geomantic figure</note> and truth, or what is deposited from one's work by a good thing, or what is accustomed to happen, are found together.

The **tenth house** is that of the kingdom and dignity, exaltation, and powers; of works, honor, and the king's power; of the leaders and primates of the kingdom. Afterwards, it pertains to the magistrate, glory, memory, and the praises of nature's lights, nobles, and inheritances. It signifies those of noble birth in high power or some signified dignity. It also signifies difficult future business that has been taken away, and the perfection of your affairs starting for utility; it signifies the whole without end.

The **eleventh house** is that of friends and friendship. It signifies reason, glory, honor, and the opportunity for the king himself, and the returning of tribute. Then, following the king, it signifies soldiers or infantry, or some power according to others. Then, truly, it is the house of hope, certain and forgiving.

The **twelfth house** is that of enemies and their cunning, and of horses and the four animals <note>likely referring to livestock or beasts of burden</note>; the lamentation of the Lord, labors, sorrows, theft, deceit, envy, detractions, and wickedness in a foreign place. Or it signifies envy in wakefulness, poverty, and power; and he feared punishments, and discoveries, and <term>writing tablets</term> <note>original: "tabulettas car[tas]"</note>.

<column-break/>

It signifies anxious messages and distresses to be placed. These are according to that astronomy, but **geomancy** <note>The art of divination by lines and points on the earth</note> has added divine things <margin>137</margin> to the rising <note>original: "de leuante"</note> called the place of origin from the **Head of the Dragon** <note>The North Node of the Moon, considered lucky</note>. Through the fulfillment of the prophecy, it is from Jupiter and the Moon in triple signs; it pertains to princes and primates, and thus provides for the happiness of the lord. On the opposite side is its own sign in the one which is called the origin from the **Tail of the Dragon** <note>The South Node of the Moon, considered unlucky</note>, which is from Saturn and Mars, for heretics, where the triple signs lead to destruction; and so it is called "all-mixing" <note>original: "michia," likely a corruption of a Greek or Arabic term for mixing/confusion</note>.

The anxious thing, as our affirmation has testified, is the truth, because in this chapter they bring forth—if God wills—it indicates and will appear.

It must be known, however, that some houses are **strong**, some are **succeeding**, and some are called **weak**. The strong ones are these: 1, 4, 7, and 10 <note>The "Angles" or cardinal points of the chart</note>. The succeeding ones are mediocre: 2, 5, 8, and 11. The weak or **falling** <note>original: "cadentes"</note> are 3, 6, 9, and 12. They are called strong because they signify something stable and immobile in a worthy sign. The succeeding ones are mediocre, which follow the strong in strength and hold the middle ground between the strong and the weak. But they are called weak because they signify something less noble and unstable; they are called "falling" because they fall away from the angles (the strong houses). Having been snatched by some force, they lose their power. If a sign is stable, mobile, or mediocre, and is in a strong house, it holds its power immobile; if it is in the succeeding houses, it holds; but if it is in the falling houses, even a strong sign changes through the weakness of the lord. Because the strong houses truly achieve the greatest victory.

<margin>Note on the angles of astronomy</margin>
Since, however, they are called such, they all revolve upon the hinges <note>Latin: *cardines*, the four pivotal points of a chart</note> in this way; in these houses there is strength because they stand in their own sign. These strengths are called **angles**. Clearly, the first house is the **Eastern Angle**, because the sign found there is directly related to the East. The second is the **Southern Angle**, because the sign then stands in the middle <note>the Midheaven</note>. The third is the **Western Angle**, because its sign is placed opposite the West. The fourth is the **Lower Angle** <note>Latin: *centriloptinet*, likely a corruption of *Imum Coeli*</note> which holds the 10th house of heaven <note>The scribe appears to be numbering or ordering these specifically for a geomantic layout</note> because it holds the middle of heaven under the opposite angle. Therefore, the boundary of the angles which geomancy <term>Geomancy: a method of divination using earth/dots, here mapped onto astrology</term> follows is based on the **triplicities**.

<unclear>Just as</unclear> in astronomy there are four signs coordinated in nature which constitute one triplicity, so in geomancy one figure in one conjunction from one triplicity creates one effect. In astronomy, however, **Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius** make the first triplicity. Each of these signs is fiery, hot, and dry, bitter in taste. The second triplicity is constituted of **Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn**, which are signs of the earth, cold and dry, melancholic in temperament, and <insert>from Adam</insert> <note>possibly a reference to the "earthy" nature of man</note>. The third triplicity is **Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius**, which are airy signs, hot and moist, sanguine, and sweet in taste. The fourth triplicity is **Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces**, which are aquatic signs, cold and moist, phlegmatic, and salty in taste. The first triplicity of signs relates to royal friendship and the quantity of the body, finite morals, and wealth. The second triplicity is that which conquers signs of knowledge and almost always governs judgment, and shows the nature of the person

<column-break/>

in the place where it is permitted to dwell, and the distance of the soul and its fortune and status, and the quantity of friends, and the solemnity or rejection of bodies. The second triplicity <note>The author is likely sub-dividing the functions of the triplicities here</note> determines the status of the sign so that it determines the middle of both. Knowledge is thus gained whether from the part of the seeker or from the part of the thing sought, demonstrating the end. If the benevolent figures are present and look upon the seeker, they will obtain what they desire, unless by chance some disagreement arises between the significators.

<margin>On Aspects</margin>
Because we have made frequent mention of **aspects**, it must now be seen what an aspect is and how many types are designated by the authors. An aspect is the emission of physical rays from one planet to another according to the movement of the signs. Hence it should be known that this aspect is from planet to planet, not from sign to sign as some used to think—unless the sign itself looks upon the signs <note>original: *nisi signum inca aspiciat signa*</note>. There are five aspects, just as a straight line is perceived by the eye. <note>The text here becomes dense with abbreviations regarding the Sun (☉) and the movement of the signs</note>. For there are "quincunx" signs which do not look at one another <note>signs that are 150 degrees apart were traditionally considered "averted" or unable to "see" each other</note>. The second is the **hexagonal** aspect or **sextile**; the **tetragonal** or **quartile** <note>square</note>; the **trigonal** or **trine**; and the **hexagonal** which is from the third sign.

### On all those things which are asked

# On Inquiries Regarding Journeys or Long Travel

The same is asked concerning a journey or a long distance. If the figure in the First House <note>The First House represents the querent, or the person asking the question.</note> is a "moving" or mobile sign, then it signifies movement. If it is a stable sign, it signifies a long stay. 

-> <note>original: Fortuna Minor</note> **Fortuna Minor** <-
<image-desc>geomantic figure: 1 dot, 2 dots, 2 dots, 1 dot</image-desc>

If the figure is found in any of the points where the Lord of the Change <note>The planetary ruler or dominant figure governing the transition.</note> was similarly moved, it signifies that the person will either stay or the sign will be weak. Then he flees movement. 

-> <note>original: Fortuna Major</note> **Fortuna Major** <-
<image-desc>geomantic figure: 2 dots, 1 dot, 1 dot, 2 dots</image-desc>

But if it is in a "moving" state, it signifies movement in the First House, or in the First and Second Houses. **Fortuna Major** <image-desc>geomantic figure: 2 dots, 1 dot, 1 dot, 2 dots</image-desc> here helps so that it may be firm, just as **Fortuna Major** signifies movement after a long time through the mobile signs. In all these things, by the evacuation of the houses <note>A technical term in geomancy referring to how figures pass from one house to another.</note>, it similarly signifies movement, but after a long time. If it is done moderately, the movement is conquered and it persists, or in moderation it is slower. In mobile signs, the angles signify movement. 

It is not through the "Tail" <note>referring to Cauda Draconis, the Dragon's Tail, usually a malefic sign</note> when the signs of movement go out into the middle or the retrogradations, as we have said; they signify movement of a longer time than the preceding. Likewise, it is through the "Tail" if the signs of movement go out from the firm or fixed signs, or through the "Tail" itself as we have said; they signify movement, but in a greater time than the preceding. If, however, in the first middle, the figures or the mediators were direct, they "tail" <note>follow or conclude</note> those going out; they signify movement of the greater ones which precede. If they are mobile in the turn, they will be heard as direct, as those going out signify movement in a greater time than the preceding. 

Likewise, it is through the "Tail" when they go out from a fixed sign into the middle of the mobile ones; they are heard as direct, as those going out signify movement then with a moderate delay. If they are in the middle of the turn, they "tail" as direct, as is the case; those going out signify movement with the greatest delay. Truly, if the figures of the houses go out from the part of the angles <note>The cardinal houses: 1, 4, 7, and 10</note> and are in a fixed sign, and the rest are "tailing" and going out in a fixed sign, it signifies no movement at all. This is expressed through the middle of these "tails"; you will find it and you shall not doubt.

In this, he will not have the best, and there will be journeys or changes. But if the figures in the Third House were in themselves entering from anxiety to happiness, the reason for which he acts is not for love, but to join with some lord or noble man, or a lord in the country.

For masculine signs signify males, and feminine signs signify females. In the end, the man will escape the sea if the signs are fortunate; if not, they will aggravate him.

As was stated above <note>original: "supi' d'm est," an abbreviation for "superius dictum est"</note>, regarding navigation, one should know whether the journey is by sea or by land. However, we shall show where the signs are located in those houses and how they are joined.

If **aquatic signs** appear, they denote a journey by sea. If they are **fiery signs**, they indicate a journey by land. This is according to the reliable theory <note>original: "fida teoz," likely referring to "theorica," the theoretical framework of astrology</note> of the signs which have these qualities in their nature. 

If aquatic signs abound <note>original: "hūidauit," likely "abundaverit"</note>, it signifies a time of travel by sea. If fiery signs abound, it signifies travel by land. And if the journey is made by sea, one must beware lest a fiery sign be in the "mouth" <note>This refers to the cusp or opening of the house being interpreted.</note> of the signs, for it corrupts and hinders the journey. If this occurs, sea-raiders <note>original: "idiatores marini," referring to pirates or privateers</note> will appear, or enemies will capture the ship. 

If, however, the signs are quiet and joined with **airy signs**, they foretell corruption by the harshness of the winds. If they are joined with **earthy signs**, they foretell delays on land <note>original: "t'and' i' u tēm t'r'is," likely "tarditatem in viis terris"</note> and signify the loss of the ship. If they are impeded, they speak of slowness of movement. But if they are among the favorable signs, it signifies a journey accelerated by sea.

Inquire here whether it is a fortunate journey or a change of location for the sign in the house. Note that if the sign is changed in any part, or if the change occurs in their own places or in receptive places <note>In astrology, a "receptive" place is one where a planet or sign is welcomed by the "lord" of that house.</note>, the journey will be fortunate. A change of journey is better when one reaches the place to which one goes. If the signs with which they are joined become better than those from which they began, the journey is good. If the signs from which one departed were better, then the journey will be difficult.

<column-break/>

If the signs in the house toward which one is moving are better than the previous signs, the journey or change is fortunate. For the signs that follow are stronger and better, and the change of journey will be praiseworthy. If, however, the previous signs were better, then the station of the body <note>original: "statiū corp'is," referring to the physical presence or health of the traveler</note> in the place where one is is better than the place to which one is going. 

The station of the body is more favored by light in the place to which one goes if the signs are better there than in the place where one had been dwelling. If the signs in the house of the destination are stronger and better, the state of the body will be better upon arrival. 

If the sign and the house are common <note>original: "com' sigū," likely meaning a "mutable" or "common" sign like Gemini or Virgo</note> or if they are weak, the destination will be less praiseworthy than the place where one currently is, and the body will be in a state of weakness. If the signs indicate the glory or fame of the journey, and the signs are strong, it will be a heavy journey for the sake of good fortune or a great house. 

Regarding the nature of the places: 
*   **Moon signs** <note>original: "lāna," likely a transcription of "Luna"</note> or other similar indicators signify places that are very obscure, defective, and unclean. 
*   **Ancient waters** <note>original: "antiq' aq̄"</note> and low-lying ways or marshy lands are indicated by these signs. 
*   If **aquatic signs** appear in a place of water or humidity, they signify much water or fluid, or perhaps worldly craftsmanship or things pertaining to the water.
*   If the signs are **hot and humid**, they signify humid, plentiful, and delightful places.

## On whether one shall have offspring

If anyone seeks to know whether they should have offspring <note>original: "plem[m]"/prolem</note> from God, and a fortunate sign appears, such as **Via** (The Way), **Albus** (White), **Conjunctio** (Conjunction), or **Puella** (The Girl) <image-desc>geomantic figures: Via, Albus, Conjunctio, Puella</image-desc>, or if a joining of some of these figures occurs, it indicates that they mitigate the lack of offspring. If it is delayed after some time, but many are generated, one will rejoice. If the significators are among the benevolent ones, he shall have offspring. 

There will also come an announcement from signs such as **Rubeus** (The Red), **Puer** (The Boy), **Amissio** (Loss), or **Acquisitio** (Gain) <image-desc>geomantic figures: Rubeus, Puer, Amissio, Acquisitio</image-desc>. These signs signify fertility in whatever time they appear. For signs of acquisition or affirmation announce success, while signs of negation are judged by what they bring to the significators. If the affirmative signs confirm, they grant it; if the negative signs deny, they refuse it. If a firm sign is received among many, he will have offspring. If nothing is received, he will have no offspring. If the matter is referred to a benevolent sign, even if it is received in part, it signifies the same. If the significator is overcome in some general part, let him be received by the type that has good fortune; but if it is corrupted by something, he will only rejoice in some part.

If someone who is not a husband asks whether he might impregnate a woman <note>original: "cum uxore", literally "with a wife," but here meaning any woman in the context of the question</note>, the first sign is considered. If three signs in the question are fortunate, there will be joy and conception will occur; if she is not impregnated then, she will not be impregnated thereafter. 

Similarly, if one asks whether the offspring <note>original: "xp̃e", likely a shorthand for "prole" or "fruit"</note> should be healthy or is in danger, examine the strength of the sign carefully. If there is a certain acceptance, or if he dismisses her, the sign will respond according to the woman who asked. 

If anyone asks whether a woman is pregnant, look at the first sign to see if it is in the house of the question or if both are present together; if so, the woman is indeed pregnant. If a woman asks this herself, the signs will confirm it. Elijah and others <note>A reference to historical or legendary authorities in the divinatory arts</note> testify to have experienced this as true.

If it is asked whether she shall bear a male or a female, look at the nature of the signs. If they are <term>fiery or airy signs</term> <note>In astrology and geomancy, Fire and Air are considered masculine elements</note>, she will bring forth a male. If they are <term>earthy or watery signs</term> <note>Earth and Water are considered feminine elements</note>, she will bear a female. If the signs are mixed, look to the one that is stronger; if it is airy or fiery, a male; if earthy or watery, she will bear a female.

She will not give birth without difficulty unless the sign of the matter is "mobile" <note>Signs that suggest movement or change</note> and free from "malice" <note>unfavorable astrological influences</note>. If the sign of Venus is present, it may bring a delivery without labor, leading to ease and relief. However, "firm" or "fixed" signs confirm a more difficult labor. If the sign is joined in its own house, or if the sign is malevolent, it will be very bad and even

mortal. This is especially true if the sign does not finish its course or if a disease occurs before she gives birth. If the sign of the <term>Fish</term> <note>original: "piscati", referring to the sign of Pisces or the geomantic figure Rubeus/Puer in a watery placement</note> appears, which is often a mortal sign in these matters, then fear is falsely instilled. But if the signs are fortunate, she will escape danger. 

If the signs are unfortunate, it signifies a hardness or a slowness of the matter. It may affirm a stillbirth <note>original: "mortuae"</note> or a miscarriage <note>original: "abortiuu"</note> through the emission of blood. ### On Lost Property
If anyone asks about something they have lost, look to the seeker and their sign. If the sign is changed at the end, or if it is in a certain point which they judge to be their own, or if it has come to that point <note>This refers to geomantic "houses" or positions in a divination chart</note>, the item will be found.

### On Fugitives and Captives
If the inquiry is about a fugitive, a loss, or a captive, see if the sign is appropriate. Assign the first sign to the seeker and the second to the fugitive. If the signs are joined, the seeker will find him through his own effort. If the sign is in another house <note>original: "in quaestione"</note>, the fugitive himself will return to the seeker. If the sign is in another part entirely, it signifies that many people are following the fugitive and he will be caught. If no one is following him, he will be found through a messenger or a letter sent between them. If the sign indicates it, the fugitive will be captured in a boat or a ship.

<image-desc>Geomantic figure: Via (four single dots in a vertical line)</image-desc> 
You shall judge according to each sign according to the power <note>original: "potestate"</note> of the sign.

### On the Manumission of Servants
If someone asks whether a servant or captive is to be manumitted <term>manumitted: the formal act of a master freeing a slave</term> by his master, attend to the signs. If they are favorable, it indicates they will be released from 

<image-desc>Geomantic figure: Populus (eight dots in four pairs)</image-desc> 
or 
<image-desc>Geomantic figure: Carcer (a "prison" shape: one dot, two dots, two dots, one dot)</image-desc> 
without delay or hardship. If the signs are found in a state of hesitation, freedom is signaled but it will happen after a long delay. If the signs are firm <note>Fixed or "stable" figures in geomancy usually suggest a lack of change</note>, they entirely deny freedom. If the sign of the Seeker is in some other part, judge that freedom will come after a period of delay.

<column-break/>

They will be released, provided that the sign is not malevolent. If it is malevolent, the master will not release him of his own will. Malevolent signs are such as:

<image-desc>Row of four geomantic figures: Cauda Draconis (the Dragon's Tail), Puer (the Boy), Amissio (Loss), and Rubeus (the Red)</image-desc>

These signify iniquity, pride, or greed, and he will not be freed. In the case of these signs, they are firm signs of non-release. If they are in another part and are much changed, they deny freedom. However, if they are changed in a favorable way, they promise freedom after a temporal delay, and such signs are to be praised for the prospect of liberty. Mobile signs <note>Figures that suggest movement and change</note> generally promise total freedom.

<margin>Regarding a servant or handmaid...</margin>
In the matter of retaining or recovering property, look to the seeker and the signs. If they are fortunate, the thing sought will be obtained. If the sign is 

<image-desc>Geomantic figure: Conjunctio (two dots, one dot, one dot, two dots)</image-desc> 
it is not to be praised, because it demonstrates a loss of profit. If the sign is 

<image-desc>Geomantic figure: Tristitia (two dots, two dots, two dots, one dot)</image-desc> 
it is a malevolent sign, signifying a deceiver or a traitor. If other mobile signs appear, it will not be praiseworthy because the result lasts only a short time.

### On Purchasing
If you wish to know whether the purchase of something will be successful, look to the seeker and the sign. If they are good, firm, and favorable, the purchase will be useful and suitable. If the signs are mobile, the purchase will be useless. If the sign 

<image-desc>Geomantic figure: Albus (two dots, two dots, one dot, two dots)</image-desc> 
is the significator, it indicates infidelity, mortality, or evil.

**Column 1**

...they extend; if Aries ♈️ or Libra ♎️ ends [the house], it signifies devotion and piety <note>This likely refers to the character of a servant being freed, continuing the topic from the previous page</note>. ### On Buying Animals
If anyone wishes to buy any animal, let them seek whether it will be a benefit. Look to the **Sixth House** <note>In traditional astrology, the Sixth House governs small animals and domestic livestock</note>. If Aries ♈️ or Leo ♌️ is present at that hour, and if the house ends or is in aspect with its Lord, it will be fast or slow... the head and the hindquarters <note>original: "pondo," likely referring to the weight or rear of the animal</note> are the stronger members, though they will be baser than the front parts. If the form is sharp and crooked, or they proceed crookedly, the feet or the evils of disease will be present, such as **gout** <term>podagra: a painful swelling of the joints, here referring to animal joint diseases</term> and humors. If it is livestock, it will be a sign of standing [illness] and mortality.

If Gemini ♊️ or Sagittarius ♐️ are in the "head" [of the chart], the hand will be eased, but the joint will have some rupture. Gemini ♊️ or Sagittarius ♐️ also signify diseases of the head and inflammation or swelling. If it is livestock, it demonstrates their debility and destruction. If any of these signs are in the animal's residence: if it is an **Earth** sign, they will be heavy and somewhat sluggish; if **Water**, they show the beast to be fat and strong. If livestock are fat and healthy, they show that they will be fruitful. If their disease comes from an abundance of the **blood humor**, the animal will be fiery, furious, lean, and wild...

<column-break/>

**Column 2**

...for men it will be strong and good for nourishing, and fast; these are the livestock that will be fruitful in hand. Their disease will come from an abundance of **choler** <note>original: "ex colū"; choler or yellow bile was the humor associated with fire and irritability</note>. If it is an **Aquatic** sign, it will be somewhat fat and weak to keep alive; the nature of their disease will come mostly from an abundance of wind <note>original: "ex flatū"; likely referring to bloating or respiratory issues</note>. If they are prosperous, they will be good and fruitful. If they are of a mixed nature, hold to whichever sign has the greater proportion in the chart; do not hesitate to judge specifically.

### On the Health of Animals
If anyone asks whether their animals are healthy, look to the first sign and then look to the **Sixth House**. If fortunate signs are in the 6th or 12th houses and safe from "unfortunate" influences <note>original: "ifortunūs"; refers to malefic planets like Mars or Saturn</note>, they will be healthy. Another sign is unfortunate, such as Aries ♈️, Libra ♎️, Cancer ♋️, or Capricorn ♑️; in sickness, these indicate either death or the devouring of limbs. If the **Moon** <note>original: "lona"</note> is poorly placed, part of them is devoured and part is alive. If the signs are **mobile** <term>mobile signs: also known as Cardinal signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), which indicate change, movement, or sudden events</term>, it predicts their loss and annihilation.

### On Lost Animals
Regarding what shall happen to a lost animal, seek from the relation of Aries ♈️ and the beast. If it was of great value or far off—or if it is a horse, a beast of burden, or a large animal—assign it to the **Twelfth House** <note>The Twelfth House traditionally governs "large cattle" or animals larger than a goat</note>. Attend to whether it is received in the 6th or 12th; let him seek it with study and labor, and he will find the union of the beasts.

If anyone asks concerning a lost animal whether he will recover it, look to the first sign and the 6th or 12th house (sometimes the 5th). If they are joined, it signifies recovery; if separated, it shall not be recovered. If certain signs are present, it signifies some tumor or [nodule] or cartilage.

### On Theft and Stolen Goods

**Robbery and theft are judged** by the place in which the theft is hidden. If it was in Jupiter, Venus, or the Sun or Moon, there was vigilance. If it was in the power of Mercury, Venus, or the Moon, or in Jupiter and Venus, then the theft will be found. 

But if it is in the territory of Saturn, the robbery will not be found, nor will the thief. If the significator of the robbery was in Saturn and they were not conquered, the robbery remains hidden. If the sign was in the Sun or Moon, no power can see it in any part <note>original: "nulla" in margin</note>, because the significator was [obscured]. 

Judge in this way whether any theft was found among them or not. If the signs of Jupiter, Venus, and the Sun are in <term>exaltation</term> <note>A state where a planet's influence is most powerful</note>, as said above, you will find neither the thief nor the stolen goods.

**It is asked whether it happened in the house or outside.** Look to the second house. If it is found in Jupiter or any other part, it happened outside. If it was from his own house, it was not outside, nor is it in the house, or he himself is hiding in the house.

## Whether you wish to know if the thief is from the house
Search among those living in the house. If any sign is found in the 4th house, it signifies that the thief is among the inhabitants of the house. ## Whether he is found where he goes
When someone asks about a person in another house, if he goes to the end or to a birth <note>referring to a destination or a relative</note>, give the 7th house. From this, understand clearly that if signs of stability are found, he will be found in that place. If he is found in the 5th house, it signifies his arrival. If it is in such a part where all the signs or their neighbors become favorable, he will be found, even if not in the place where it was believed. He delights that if the road leads, he will reach rest.

## Therefore, whether it is better to stay or to leave
Assign the 1st house to staying. If the 1st house shows better and more praiseworthy signs, then staying is more to be praised than leaving. If better signs are in the 7th or 10th houses, you shall judge accordingly.

## Therefore, whether there is stability between two
Pay attention to the 1st, 7th, 2nd, and 10th houses. If the signs are productive, it confirms a journey or mobile possessions in that part of the land.

## Concerning the participation of two or three
In the matter which concerns them, assign the 1st house to the seeker. If benevolent signs are in the 1st, 2nd, 7th, or 8th, signs of acquisition will be praiseworthy, and the participation will be a profitable transaction for both sides. If the signs are quiet and received... but if they are malevolent in the 1st, 2nd, 7th, or 8th, judge it as a loss. The one who has the better ruler will be judged to have the profit. But if <image-desc>geomantic figure Populus: dots arranged 2, 2, 2, 2</image-desc> **Populus** appears, it signifies a lack of foresight, greed, avarice, and envy, with labor and delay.

## How to Know a Person's Name
If you wish to know someone's name, set out the figures according to the matter at hand. The first figure represents the beginning of the name, the second is the middle, and the third is the end.

## On the Nativity of a Person
If you wish to know someone’s birth <term>nativitas</term> <note>The astrological conditions at the moment of birth</note>, set out the figure and see which figure it is in the chart. By the nature of the figure and the day of the questioning, identify the sign and the planet. If that planet is present, and if two figures are joined in the sign, then if the first figure of that figure is on the day [of birth], he was born at the beginning of the sign; if it is at the end of the sign, he was born at the end of that sign.

## On the Most Powerful Judgment
Note that the most powerful judgment is obtained if the first figure signifies that which is in the seeker's <term>voluntas</term> <note>The desire or specific intent of the person asking the question</note> in the 5th, 2nd, or 3rd houses, or at the end in the 1st or 9th. For if the figure is found in the 1st house and is not hindered, it is doubled, as is the figure.

## On Travelers by Sea or River
If you wish to know concerning those navigating on the sea or rivers: if in the 1st house there is :: <note>The figure *Carcer* (Prison), signifying restriction or delay</note> or :: <note>The figure *Conjunctio* (Conjunction) or another similar pattern</note>, or if these appear in the 1st or 10th houses, they are an evil sign. They signify loss through greed or the destruction of the vessel <note>original: "nāuigiū frange"</note>.

## On Firm Possessions
If you wish to know whether a possession will be firm and held with prosperity—whether it concerns taxes, servants, or any other possession—let a judgment be made. See what figure arrives in the House of Fortune <note>The 2nd house of a geomantic chart, governing wealth and assets</note>. If the figure arrives in the su-

<column-break/>

-preme will <note>referring to the top of the geomantic shield</note> and is good, and it is likewise a good sign in the house of giving, and the Judge <term>iudex</term> <note>The 15th figure in a geomantic chart, which provides the final answer</note> comes out well or is properly situated, then it shall be acquired.

## On the Fertility of the Seasons
If you wish to know about the abundance and fertility of the seasons—whether the current time will be productive or not—let a judgment be made by the sign that arrives in the House of Fortune. If there is a good sign in the supreme will and the Judge is found to be good, this season will be abundant. If, however, the sign was very good but the Judge was bad, judge the first part of the season to be good but the remainder to be not so good. Indeed, seek all things from the Judge.

## On Hidden Thoughts
From the figures and the form of the figures, take one as a sign of the seeker's intent. Thus, find that figure in the question; it will judge what shall be. Regarding what is signified by the doubling of a figure: if you find it in the question, it has a hidden meaning. Some say that through this, it shall be judged what is to come of the question.

Another method: if the first and third figures represent a thought about a matter that can turn out well, then if he thought of a matter that can be gained... <insert>or handled</insert>. And if it doubles itself in the 2nd house, he thinks of a gift or gain; if in the 3rd, of brothers or relatives; if in the 4th, of the father or an inheritance. Thus it goes for the others, until the end. If the figure is doubled, or if it is a time of thought concerning an angle, or of a journey, or of letters.

<margin>goodness and badness / and cessation</margin>
The goodness or badness of the judged resolution depends on this: whether it is emptied of all other things. It is compared to the Moon, which separates itself from one planet and joins another in its lunation through all the signs and degrees. Therefore, a "13" <note>referring to the 13th house or the First Witness</note> is given for the one from which the Moon separates, and a "14" <note>the Second Witness</note> for the one it joins. If the 13th is good, it is a good sign; if it is bad, it tends toward the worse. But if the 14th is bad, it is bad; if it is good, it tends toward the better. And if these are good, the outcome will be good; if bad, bad. If one is good and the other bad, it shall be judged as a mediocre or mixed result.

<margin>concerning the 16 figures</margin>
The true significance of the **16 figures** must be considered. Because if a figure is good and it duplicates in any place, then every sign that precedes the recipient will be for the good. But if it is bad, an evil or misfortune will happen according to the property of that sign. And if it is good and does not duplicate itself, a certain good will come from mercy; if it is bad, likewise.

<margin>on arrival</margin>
The **arrival** of the same matter must be considered as to whether it is fast or slow, which is recognized thus: calculate all the points of the 16 figures. If they are more than 96—since all the figures consist of that many points <note>16 figures multiplied by an average of 6 points equals 96; this is a mathematical check of the entire chart</note>—the arrival 

<column-break/>

will be slow. And the more points there are, the slower the arrival will be. And as much as they are less than 96, the sooner and faster it will be. If there are exactly 96, then it will be neither fast nor slow.

<margin>joys</margin>
The **joys** of the planets are also to be noted. For certain figures rejoice in certain houses: the figures of *Mercury* <note>original: "m̄ortī," likely a scribal error for Mercury</note> rejoice in the **Ascendant** <note>the 1st house</note>; figures of the **Moon** in the 3rd; **Venus** in the 4th; **Mars** in the 5th; the **Sun** in the 9th; **Jupiter** in the 11th; and **Saturn** in the 12th. And when a figure is in its own joy, its goodness is doubled; and if it should be bad, its malice is doubled.

<margin>aspects</margin>
**Aspects** <note>the geometric angles between figures</note> must be considered. Because if it is a good figure in a sextile or trine aspect <note>original: "6. u' l' tiō," referring to the 60-degree and 120-degree favorable angles</note> from the Ascendant, it is good. Otherwise not, because the aspect is weakened or absent. Likewise, it must be seen what the figure alone signifies; for if it is good and it rises from a good place and is joined to a good place, its goodness is increased. If it is bad, it is diminished. And if it is good and born from a good place, the good will be more complete. But if one is bad and the other good, it remains in its own original significance.

<margin>prohibition</margin>
**Prohibition** occurs when two significators are joined in such a way that one of them is fortunate and the other unfortunate. If the first is unfortunate, he will not obtain the thing because of his own hindrance. And if the other is also unfortunate, it prohibits the matter entirely. But if both are fortunate, the figures will bring about a completion. Many bad things hinder the matter, and the same figures which were in a multitude of significations—if they were bad—will easily cause a prohibition, if not in total, then in part.

<meta>This page transitions from the physical descriptions of geomantic figures to the underlying astrological principles that govern them. To what was previously said, I arrange the divinity <note>original: "divinitatem," referring to the divine order or perhaps "diversity" of the heavens</note> of the superior motions. For the power of the signs and the qualities of our planets are essential. Therefore, with the eyes of the aforementioned, let us look toward the divine presence through the revolution [of the spheres].

There are 12 signs, which are distinguished by our aforementioned names: Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius are fiery by nature, being hot and <gloss>dry</gloss>. Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn are cold <gloss>and</gloss> dry. Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius are airy, which are hot <gloss>and</gloss> moist. Scorpio, Pisces, [and Cancer] <note>Cancer is omitted here but implied by the grouping</note> are watery, being cold <gloss>and</gloss> moist. 

The natures of the planets are as follows: **Saturn** is extremely cold and dry; just as things that do not live of themselves are foul, he does not restore heat or moisture. **Jupiter** is extremely friendly by nature; however, he possesses more heat than moisture. **Mars**, if situated with dryness, does not tolerate reason because of his dominant nature; however, he possesses more heat than dryness. **The Sun**, truly the representative of heat, lacks nothing; from him, all qualities proceed in extreme excellence. **Venus** is moderately hot and superfluously moist. Whence she is the mother <note>original: "fex," likely a contraction for "genitrix" or "source"</note> of all fruits and sexual pleasures. **Mercury** identifies his nature according to the aspect <note>The geometric relationship between planets</note> he shares with other planets; nevertheless, he is in himself cold <gloss>and</gloss> dry. **The Moon** is said to be not moderately cold and extremely moist; whence she is called the source of moisture, just as the Sun is the source of heat. Yet, she is compared to heat as well.

These aforementioned signs have certain dignities <gloss>not</gloss> attributed by many, which are ruling powers <gloss>reigning</gloss>. They are evidence [of strength], such as: Domicile, Exaltation, Triplicity, Term, and Face. Almost every planet has 5 strengths <term>fortitudes</term> <note>These are "essential dignities," a scoring system used by medieval astrologers to determine how powerful a planet is in a specific degree of the zodiac.</note>:
**Domicile** [House] gives 5;
**Exaltation** gives 4;
**Triplicity** gives 3;
**Term** gives 2;
**Face** gives only 1.
Whence we say <gloss>not</gloss> that the planet is strong in itself through [just] any one of these, but in its accumulation. And therefore, the Domicile is found in one's own character and reasoning; Exaltation is found in one’s kingdom and glory; Triplicity in one's honor. These are not without helpers <gloss>in this</gloss>.

This is like being among one's own kin in a lineage. A planet in its **Face** is like being in its own mastery or office. A good **Aspect** is like having common friends; a bad **Aspect** is like an enemy.

The **Exaltations** of the planets are these: 
The **Sun** is exalted in **Aries**. 
The **Moon** in **Taurus**. 
**Saturn** in **Libra**. 
**Jupiter** in **Cancer**. 
**Mars** in **Capricorn**. 
**Venus** in **Pisces**. 
**Mercury** in **Virgo**. 

Just as in Aries the Sun is exalted by a single virtue, so in Libra he is in his fall <note>original: "deotioio," likely "deiectio," meaning fall or depression</note>, which is the sign opposite to Aries.

The **Domiciles** [Houses] of the planets are the signs in which they were created <note>According to the "Thema Mundi," the mythical birth chart of the universe</note>: 
**Leo** is the house of the **Sun**. 
**Cancer** of the **Moon**. 
**Virgo** of **Mercury**. 
**Libra** of **Venus**. 
**Aries** of **Mars**. 
**Sagittarius** of **Jupiter**. 
**Scorpio** is also assigned to [Mars]. 
Note that they have accidental powers in four signs of retention.

**Jupiter** is also in **Pisces**. 
**Mars** in <gloss>for example</gloss> **Taurus**. 
**Venus** in **Taurus**. 
**Mercury** in **Gemini**. 
Whence these are accidental reasons.

**Triplicity** occurs when a planet is in a sign of the same quality as the sign in which it was created. For example, when the **Sun** is in **Sagittarius** or in **Aries**, which are hot and dry signs like **Leo**, in which it was created. 
And the **Moon** when she is in **Scorpio** or **Pisces**, which are cold and moist signs like **Cancer**, in which her lordship is given.

Thirdly: The active planets served the aforementioned divisions. They are the moist ones and the masters of those who are moist. **Jupiter** has these; he is the author. **Venus**, the mother of followers, and so on, as appears in this table.

**The Faces or radiating signs**

The <term>Faces</term> <note>also known as Decans</note> are divided in turn. Each of the signs is divided into three equal parts of 10 degrees each, which are called "Faces" or by the name "Decans." A Face is that through which the planet ascends. The first Face is from 0 to 10 degrees, the second from 10 to 20, and the third from 20 to 30. For example, in the beginning of Aries, the Face belongs to Mars <note>This follows the "Chaldean" order of planets: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon</note>. Here he gives them in order as in the table above.

**Planetary Aspects**

These are the testimonies that the planets receive, as some are valid <term>strengths</term> <note>fortitudines</note> and others are <term>weaknesses</term> <note>debilitates</note>. They receive these mutually from one another. Thus, through a "good" aspect, a planet receives strength from another; through a "bad" aspect, it receives weakness. 

There are 4 types of aspects: 
1. **Opposition**
2. **Quartile** <note>now commonly called a Square</note>
3. **Trine**
4. **Sextile**

The aspect of **Opposition** <note>180 degrees apart</note> or when planets are in such a position, is called the worst aspect, especially if the planets are naturally divergent <note>meaning their qualities conflict</note>. For instance, if Venus is in Aries and Saturn is in Libra. This is the same for other configurations where planets are in the same degree.

---

Here he speaks of the reality of the signs through the planets. An aspect exists when there is a specific distance between two planets in the signs. For example, when the Sun is in Aries and Saturn is in Libra, they are in opposition. This aspect is called "evil" or "unfortunate."

The **Trine** <note>120 degrees apart</note> aspect is when two planets are in similar signs <note>signs belonging to the same element, like Fire or Water</note> which contain within themselves a firm trinity. This aspect is the best, as it is not found in conflicting qualities of the signs. Therefore, if there were two planets, such as Jupiter and Venus, in a trine aspect, nothing but good would follow.

The **Sextile** <note>60 degrees apart</note> aspect is when there are two signs in the middle between two planets. This is considered a moderate or "middling" aspect. 

Finally, a **Conjunction** <note>original: "Cōperiet" likely for "Conjunctio"</note> is when two planets are in the same degree. Astrologers call this the strongest influence. We, however, find much significance in the opposition aspect as well.

<margin>
Many aspects.
In many aspects they see each other.
</margin>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of celestial mechanics and their physical effects on Earth, moving from the geometry of planetary orbits to the specific influence of the Moon on the tides, and how to calculate planetary "testimonies" for astrological judgment.</meta>

->**The Southern Moon and the Tides**<-

The moon in its southern inclination <note>original: "aplinati meridionale"; likely referring to the moon's declination or its position relative to the celestial equator</note>, when it wanes, it reduces the **swelling** <note>original: "tumore"; a common medieval term for the tidal bulge of the sea</note>. It causes the waters to rise toward the opposite side by its generative powers. It is clear that one perceives two measures of the **flow** <note>original: "fluxum"; the tide</note> in a natural day: one when the moon is positioned above the horizon, from its rising until its setting, which causes the highest point of the swelling. In the same way that the moon moves from east to west, so too does that swelling move. Now, as the moon completes its entire circuit by day and night, the swelling similarly decreases when it recedes from its **apogee** <note>original: "auge"; the highest or furthest point of an orbit</note>.

Now, when the moon is at its apogee, then the flow of the sea is greatest, even when it is in its increasing phase during that time. But when it is in the opposite position, the flow of the sea is at its minimum, as appears on day .A. of the moon .al. 12. 7. when the moon appears as a semi-circle. Now there appear the "tropics" <note>turning points</note> of the sun and moon in these lower regions; similarly in the spring rains and such. Wherefore it is clear that all planets, the further they are from their center, the stronger the influence they have in these intervals; however, the closer they are, the weaker. Their strengths vary according to their proximity to the center of the world or their distance; for when they are close, they are strong, but when they are elongated, they act more weakly.

These then are the "testimonies" <note>pieces of evidence or dignities used to weigh a planet's influence</note> of the planets, both essential <insert>ly</insert> and accidental, which are necessary for our investigation. So that all the aforesaid may be understood without labor, I have described three figures of "eyes" <note>referring to circular diagrams or focal points in a manuscript illustration</note>. The first is the eye of Figure 2, the second is called the eye... now the third, I believe, is decorated with these small orbs. The whole roundness of the eyes is divided into 12 equal parts by the distinction of the **signs** <note>the twelve signs of the Zodiac</note>. I shall place the testimonies of the planets found in each sign: first, I will place 4 [points] for **exaltation** <note>a sign where a planet's influence is heightened</note>, 2 for **triplicity** <note>a group of three signs belonging to the same element</note>, 3 for **term** <note>specific degrees of a sign ruled by a planet</note>, and 2 for a single **face** <note>a ten-degree division of a sign</note>. Now these signs remain constant. Thus, when you have recognized the disposition of the air or the continuity of the seasons, you will wish to show the position of each planet at that same time through the tables which record their testimonies.

<column-break/>

The insignias will be noted, and one will judge by the planet having more testimonies, as the disposition of that time will belong to the one with the most testimonies. For example, let the locations of the planets be noted for the year 626 of the Arabs <note>approx. 1229 AD</note>, in the month of January, on the 12th and 9th... on that day of the month which is the 11th day before the Kalends of May <note>April 21st</note>. Now the Sun is found in the 23rd degree [of Aries]. The Moon is in the 20th. Jupiter is in the sign... 14 in 20. Saturn is in the 4th degree of Aquarius, or in the 21st of Taurus. Mercury is in the 12th of Taurus, and so the Sun is in its highest temperament, and temperate for this reason. Now Jupiter in the 23rd degree of Aries is strong in its **exaltation**; hence it has 4 testimonies. In its own planet <note>its own sign</note> it has its cause. Now in this one sign it has... it is not in a worse position by any other planet, unless its nature were disposed otherwise. If Venus is the cause, she is in the 11th degree of Taurus, which is her own home, and there she has 4 testimonies. Mercury is in its own [sign?]; now it is in the 12th degree of Taurus, where it has two testimonies. Either the sign or the... has two testimonies. It should be known that the Moon stays in any given sign for 2 days and 6 hours. And it is known that when the Moon first renews <note>original: "renovat"; refers to the New Moon phase when the Moon and Sun are in conjunction</note>, it renews in the same sign in which the Sun is currently located. For example, if the Sun is currently in **Scorpio**, the Moon will stay in that sign for 2 days and 6 hours; and afterward in **Sagittarius** for 2 days and 6 hours; and afterward in **Capricorn** for 2 days and 6 hours; and afterward in **Aquarius** for 2 days and 6 hours; and afterward in **Pisces** for 2 days and 6 hours; and afterward in **Aries** for 2 days and 6 hours; and afterward in **Taurus** for 2 days and 6 hours; and afterward in **Gemini** for 2 days and 6 hours; and afterward in **Cancer** for 2 days and 6 hours; and afterward in **Leo** for 2 days and 6 hours; and afterward in **Virgo** for 2 days and 6 hours; and afterward in **Libra** for 2 days and 6 hours. These <unclear>are</unclear> the hours of the lunation <note>the cycle of the Moon's phases</note> in <unclear>one</unclear> <unclear>year</unclear>, and this calculation is used by physicians for <term>bloodletting</term> <note>original: "minutione"; the surgical removal of blood to balance the body's humors</note>, for <term>purging</term> <note>original: "purgatione"; the administration of medicines to cleanse the digestive system</note>, <unclear>and so forth</unclear>.

<meta>This page transitions from the divinatory practices of geomancy seen on the previous page to the precision of medieval astronomy and timekeeping. The focus shifts to the use of a quadrant, an instrument used to determine the time of day based on the sun's position and the observer's specific latitude. Also, from the 11th of May until the 22nd of the same—from 65 to 67
Also, from the 23rd of May until the end of the same—from 67 to 69

If you wish to know the **natural hours** <term>natural hours: also known as "unequal hours," these divide the period of daylight into 12 equal parts. Consequently, a "natural hour" is much longer in the summer than in the winter</term> on any day by means of the **quadrant** <term>quadrant: a portable medieval instrument shaped like a quarter-circle, used for measuring the height of celestial bodies to tell time or determine latitude</term>, look up the latitude of the region or the **altitude of the pole** <note>original: "altitudinem poli"; the angle of the North Star above the horizon, which corresponds to the observer's latitude</note>. For example: 
**England** is 50° 30'; 
**Paris** is 48°; 
in **Montpellier** nearly 44°; 
**Cremona** 45°; 
**Rome** nearly 42°; 
**Naples** 41°; 
**Messina** 38°; 
and **Tunis** 35°; 
**Alexandria** 31°; 
**Jerusalem** 32°. 

And count that many degrees on the **rim** <note>original: "limbo"</note> of the quadrant, starting from the right side; and where that number ends, move the **cursor** <term>cursor: a sliding bead or pointer on the instrument's string used to mark a specific calculation</term> until it is at the beginning of **Aries**—that is, the **equinoctial line** <note>original: "equinoctialis linea"; the line representing the celestial equator where the sun resides during the spring and autumn equinoxes</note> falls directly over the **plumb line** <term>plumb line: a weighted cord (pendiculum) hanging from the corner of the quadrant used as a vertical reference</term>. Thus, the cursor will be fixed for that specific region.
