If anyone should ask whether a battle <note>original: "prolium"</note> and its outcome will be fortunate or not—such as a change of location, or whether he should depart or not—look first to the **First House** <term>Ascendant|The first house of a geomantic or astrological chart, representing the person asking the question (the querent).</term>. If it is found in a suitable place, that itself will be a sign of change. If it should be a **fortune** <note>original: "fortuna"; refers to a benefic geomantic figure like Greater Fortune or Joy</note> in conjunction with good things, and located in a good house and well-received, then all the "angles" <term>cardines|The four most powerful houses in a chart (1, 4, 7, and 10), which indicate the strength of an outcome.</term> that are favored by fortune will result in a prosperous change, and his status will be better in the place to which he goes. And if the signs with which it joins are better than those from which it separates, [it is good]; conversely, if the signs from which it separates were better than those with which it joins, then the change or outcome will not be worthy of praise. 

And if the signs of the 1st house and the 8th <note>In this context, the 8th house is being used to analyze the destination or the outcome of a journey/conflict.</note> are better than the first and second signs, and the remaining angles are similarly fortunate, then the change will be lucky. I say the same regarding the 1st house; and similarly I say that if the 6 signs following it are stronger and better by themselves, the change will be praiseworthy; and I say the same for the signs previously signifying. 

And note that the form of the first sign shows his status in the place where he is, and the second sign shows his condition and how much he might know of the form and the "emptying" <note>original: "evacuacim"; likely referring to the depletion of resources or the outcome of leaving</note> in the place to which he goes. Similarly, because the 8th and 1st were the significators of the place to which he will go, thus shall his approach be, and whether good or evil happens to him. 

According to the 8th house, let him know if the gain <note>original: "lucru"</note> will be good or bad, according to the disposition of the fortunes and misfortunes of the signs and figures. Since the 1st and 8th houses are the significators of the acquisition and loss of the place to which he proposes to go: if the 1st is stronger than the prior sign and in a better state, his status will be better at the place he proposes, and vice versa. 

And if the sign of the 8th house—which represents the gain of the place to which he goes—is more fortunate and profitable than the sign of the 1st and 2nd houses, he will be **victorious** and will prevail over his enemies <note>original: "lucrabitur super inimicos suos"</note>, and vice versa. And if the 1st and 8th houses are unfortunate signs, he will receive evil and harm in the place of his enemies. And if the form is as the 2nd, a change into the 12th house—wherever that sign may be—signifies evil and detriment on his part, and vice versa.

And if he trusts in him, or <unclear>if he is a friend</unclear>, or a friend, and if he is an obedient friend and <unclear>obedient</unclear> by his work, or if the gift sought from him will be obtained.

### Chapter of Ptolemy on the method of using and practicing the works

<margin>14</margin>
After we have spoken about all the individual figures through their three houses <note>In geomancy, figures are often tracked as they "pass" from one house (a division of the chart) to another to show how a situation evolves.</note> in which our intentions may perish or find the intentions of those who bring results, we must now consider if someone should ask about the world and what is prepared—which I hope for and in which I shall find faith. It is necessary to recognize the good <note>original: "lonas," likely a transcription error for "bonas" (good).</note> figures and their rulers and their participation. For if they are among the fortunate figures and those that signify victory, and if they are joined by the "coming" houses <note>The houses that represent future developments.</note>, and he asks in what way that which he found is preserved and given life—if the figures appear even then, he shall arrive at that which he hoped for, if not in its entirety, then according to the quantity of the third figure.

And if it does not come to him, then in that matter he will be opposed, and he will refine the thing about which he has struggled; then something of it will come to him after he had [previously] not wanted it. For there are—even if all the figures are divided—those that do nothing and want nothing; <margin>h</margin> <margin>now</margin> <margin>up to here</margin> <margin>namely</margin> they acquire no power here, neither from the first nor from the last. And if all the figures are divided from that which our nature gave us, that thing will come to him through labor and the loss of hope, whether in whole or in part. <margin>that</margin> Specifically, according to the quantity of the "helping" figures from the houses and their difficulty; and according to the quantity and quality of the figures' labor, his ability and ease will be known from that difficulty and... <unclear>entering</unclear>. This is through that which is to be formed, which we have already set forth.
